description: Dietrich, Christian and colleagues publish this resource through Zenodo. The spreadsheet provides substances identified through suspect screening and database comparison in Danube-catchment samples between Vienna and Budapest. It includes corresponding peak intensities and supports the documented water-cycle monitoring and contaminant-assessment programme. These are non-target analytical signals: the source explicitly states that measured intensities are not concentrations. The collection therefore retains a separate identity from targeted PFAS concentration observations. Full sampling dates, signal normalization and detection coverage remain unspecified in the short metadata, and spreadsheet values were not opened or independently checked. Coverage is limited to the stated models, observations and application settings. Native metadata gives open access and the licence label cc-by-4.0. These terms describe the deposit; software and companion-data terms are distinguished where separately established. Only descriptive metadata and file descriptors were inspected; linked data, code and document bodies were not opened.
